Why Open-Ended is Harder Than MCQ

In MCQ, you simply identify the digestive organ. In Open-Ended, you must construct the causal chain: identifying the action (e.g., chewing into smaller pieces), applying the scientific principle (increasing surface area), and stating the outcome (faster digestion). Examiners will penalize you if any link in this chain is missing.

Common P4 Open-Ended Writing Mistakes

Avoid these common traps when writing your Human Systems answers.

Critical Distinctions for P4

Keywords to Write in Your P4 Answers

Linking Words

Use in contact with to physically link the food and the juices. Use allows to show how increased surface area causes faster digestion.

Wrong Written Answers — P4 Traps

EXPLAIN Formula

Use this when asked how a feature (like folds or chewing) helps digestion.

Real Example from a P4 Model Answer:

The folds increase the surface area of the small intestine in contact with the digestive juices. This allows food to be digested faster.
What to AVOID:
Stopping at "it breaks into small pieces" without mentioning surface area.
Using vague words like "helps it digest better" instead of "faster".

COMPARE Formula

Use this when comparing two states (e.g., small vs large pieces of food).

Real Example from a P4 Model Answer:

The smaller the size of food, the less the mass of the food left after one hour.
What to AVOID:
Only describing one side of the comparison (e.g., only talking about the small pieces).

STATE Formula

Use this to supply direct factual recall.

Real Example from a P4 Model Answer:

Digestion is the process of breaking down food into simple substances that the body can absorb and use.
What to AVOID:
Writing a long paragraph. State questions just need the exact keyword.

Universal Open-Ended Answer Checklist

✓ Did I use the words 'surface area' when chewing or cutting is involved?
✓ Did I specify that digested food is absorbed into the 'bloodstream'?
✓ Did I remember that the gullet and large intestine perform NO digestion?
✓ Did I use the term 'simple substances' when defining digestion?
✓ Did I check the graph lines to see if digestion is actually happening (line goes down)?
